record.original_question: Does there exist a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem? Here K_2 is the class of groups of 2-knots, so the question asks whether some group of a 2-knot has no algorithm deciding, for an arbitrary word in its generators, whether that word represents the identity element.

evidence.quote: Though we do not know whether 2-knot groups with unsolvable word problem exist, we prove (Corollary 3.5) that there are 3-knot groups with unsolvable word problem.
For n ≥ 0 we define Kn to be the class of groups of n-knots.
(1) Is there a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem? Conjecture: Yes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An n-knot is a smooth (or locally flat topological) embedding of the n-sphere S^n into the (n+2)-sphere S^{n+2}, considered up to ambient isotopy. The group of an n-knot K is the fundamental group π_1(S^{n+2} \ K) of the complement. A finitely generated group G is said to have solvable word problem if there exists an algorithm which, given any finite word w in a fixed finite set of generators (and their inverses), decides whether w represents the identity element of G; otherwise the word problem is unsolvable.

Question: Does there exist a 2-knot K ⊂ S^4 whose knot group π_1(S^4 \ K) has unsolvable word problem?
artifact.category_tag: High-dimensional knot groups and decision problems
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether some 2-knot group has unsolvable word problem appears to remain open. While it is known that there exist 3-knot groups with unsolvable word problem (e.g., universal 3-knot groups containing every finitely presented group), no such construction is known for 2-knots, and the problem is stated as a conjecture (expected answer: yes) in the literature on higher-dimensional knot groups.

status_evidence.title: Unsolvable problems about higher-dimensional knots and related groups
status_evidence.snippet: Though we do not know whether 2-knot groups with unsolvable word problem exist, we prove that there are 3-knot groups with unsolvable word problem.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem is stated as an open question, with a conjectured affirmative answer.

status_evidence.title: L'Enseignement Mathématique (2) 56 (2010), 143–171 — Unsolvable Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of unsolvable problems about higher-dimensional knot groups; 3-knot groups can have unsolvable word problem.
status_evidence.claim: Published version reiterates that the 2-knot case is open while the 3-knot case is settled.
